title: Bihar Property Records: New Fast-Track Digital Correction System Launched - Realty Today
article_text:
In a significant move to modernize land governance and protect homeowners, the Bihar state government has officially launched a high-speed digital mechanism to fix errors in property registration records. This initiative, introduced in May 2026, aims to resolve long-standing issues where digital data did not match physical ownership documents. By setting strict deadlines and utilizing a transparent online workflow, Bihar is making it easier for citizens to ensure their land titles are accurate and legally sound.
This new system is part of a broader digital transformation strategy. It addresses a common pain point for property owners: the frustration of finding typing errors or missing data in their online records which often leads to rejected bank loans or stalled property sales.
The Problem: Why Digital Corrections Were Needed
For years, Bihar has been working to digitize millions of physical property deeds. During this massive data entry process, manual errors were inevitable. Simple typing mistakes in names, incorrect land area measurements, or blurry scans of old documents created a gap between what the owner held in their hand and what the government computer showed.
Previously, fixing these small mistakes was a slow and exhausting process. Citizens often had to visit government offices multiple times, facing delays that lasted months or even years. The lack of a clear timeline also created opportunities for middlemen to exploit worried property owners. The new Digital Correction Mechanism removes these hurdles by introducing a time-bound, transparent, and accountable process.
Key Features of the New System
The Bihar government has released a detailed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) that officials must follow. Here are the core pillars of the new system:
1. Strict Time Limits (The 22-Day Rule) The most important feature of this update is the speed. The government has mandated that even the most complex corrections must be completed within a maximum of 22 working days. Most simple clerical errors are expected to be fixed much faster, often within 7 to 10 days.
2. Electronic Workflow and Tracking Every correction request is tracked through a digital portal. Owners can see exactly which officer is handling their file and how many days are left before the deadline. This transparency forces officials to act quickly and prevents files from getting lost on someone’s desk.
3. Clear Categories of Errors The system is designed to handle three specific types of mistakes:
Data Entry Errors: Mistakes in the name of the buyer or seller, father’s name, address, or the specific details of the land like the Khata or Khesra numbers.
Measurement Errors: Incorrect entry of the total area of the property or its boundaries.
Scanning Issues: In cases where the original deed was scanned poorly, making it unreadable or missing pages, the system allows for a high-quality re-scan and upload.
Step-by-Step: How the Correction Process Works
The government has divided the correction process into four clear stages to ensure accuracy and prevent fraud.
Stage 1: The Initial Inquiry (7 Days) Once a property owner submits a request for correction, it goes to the local registration officer. This officer has seven working days to compare the digital record with the original physical deed stored in the government archives. They must prepare a report confirming that a mistake exists.
Stage 2: Verification and Approval (7 Days) The report is then sent to a senior verifying officer. This person acts as a second pair of eyes to ensure the correction is genuine. They have seven days to check the report and give their formal approval.
Stage 3: The Formal Order (3 Days) After approval, the district-level authority must issue a formal legal order to change the digital record. This must be done within three working days.
Stage 4: Technical Update (5 Days) Finally, the technical IT team receives the order. They have five working days to log into the database and update the information. Once done, the owner receives a notification that their record is now correct.
Enhancing Security and Preventing Fraud
While speed is important, the Bihar government has also focused heavily on security. To prevent unauthorized people from changing land records, the system includes several safety layers:
Audit Trails: The system records exactly who made a change, at what time, and from which computer.
Annual IT Audits: Every year, independent experts will audit the database to ensure that all changes made were backed by a legal order.
History Preservation: The original (wrong) record is not simply deleted. It is stored in the background history so that if a dispute arises later, officials can see the entire story of how and why the record was changed.
Why This is a Game Changer for Bihar Citizens
The impact of this reform goes beyond just fixing typos. It has real-world economic benefits for millions of people.
1. Faster Bank Loans When you apply for a home loan or a gold loan against your property, banks perform a strict check of the digital records. Even a small spelling mistake in a name can cause a bank to reject the loan. This new fast-track system ensures that people can fix these issues in less than a month, allowing them to get credit when they need it most.
2. Clearer Property Sales Buying or selling land in Bihar becomes much safer when the digital records are 100 percent accurate. It reduces the chance of legal disputes and court cases, which can often drag on for decades in India.
3. Eliminating Corruption By removing the need for face-to-face meetings with officials and setting a hard deadline of 22 days, the government has taken away the power of corrupt individuals to demand extra money for doing their job.
Important Advice for Property Owners
While this system is a major step forward, property owners should keep two things in mind:
First, this system is only for correcting mistakes where the digital record does not match the physical deed. If there is a mistake on your actual physical paper document (the deed you signed years ago), you cannot use this digital fix. You will still need to go through the legal process of a correction deed.
Second, property owners are encouraged to visit the official Bihar land records portal and check their data today. Do not wait until you are in the middle of a sale or a loan application to find a mistake. Use the search tool to find your property and verify that every detail, from the spelling of your name to the size of the plot, is exactly as it should be.
Conclusion: A Model for Digital India
Bihar’s move to create a fast-track digital correction mechanism is a landmark reform in land administration. By combining technology with strict administrative accountability, the state is protecting the rights of property owners and making the real estate market more reliable.
As other states look for ways to modernize their own systems, the Bihar model of transparency, time-bound results, and digital history-keeping serves as a powerful example of how technology can be used to serve the common citizen. For the people of Bihar, the days of waiting months to fix a simple clerical error are finally over. This is a big win for ease of living and a major step toward a more prosperous and transparent state.

title: Police Expose Inter-State Cyber Fraud Network in Buxar, 18 Arrested - The420.in

Buxar: In a major blow to organised cybercrime, Buxar Police have busted a well-structured inter-state cyber fraud syndicate operating from a rented house in Bihar and arrested 18 accused. Officials describe it as one of the biggest cyber enforcement operations in the region in recent years.
Acting on a credible tip-off, teams from the Nagar Police Station and the Cyber Cell raided a secret hideout located behind the ICICI Bank building on PP Road, turning what appeared to be a residential den into a crime scene loaded with digital evidence.
Initial investigation suggests the gang was using Bihar as a low-risk operational hub while siphoning money from unsuspecting victims across India through fake digital banking assistance, UPI/OTP frauds and illegal online betting.
A Fraud Call Centre in Disguise
Police officials revealed that the setup operated much like a fake call centre, where fraudsters posed as:
- Bank officials
- Digital wallet or payment app representatives
- Gaming/betting platform executives
- Customer support agents
They lured victims into sharing their OTPs, UPI PINs, and banking credentials under the pretext of KYC updates, reward points, cashback offers, or account re-verification.
The raid led to the recovery of: 64 mobile phones, 5 laptops, 25 SIM cards, 82 ATM cards, 9 bank passbooks, 13 registers filled with victims’ data, 2 Wi-Fi routers and other gadgets. The registers contain hundreds of phone numbers and bank account details, indicating that many more victims are yet to surface.
Accused Linked to Multiple States
The arrested individuals belong to Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, several of whom are repeat offenders in cyber fraud cases. Officials believe the arrests may reveal deeper involvement of fund suppliers, SIM card providers and money mules operating across state lines.
“This is a well-oiled network. The accused used Bihar as their safe base while targeting victims nationwide,” a senior investigator said.
Police have withheld the full identities of the accused pending further verification and combined investigations with other state agencies.
Digital Surveillance and Tactical Strike
The operation was led by DySP and Cyber Police Station In-charge, who confirmed that the crackdown was the result of:- Mobile location tracing, Analysis of suspicious transaction trails, Interception of coordinated calls, Support from cyber forensic intelligence. The raid was executed as a surprise tactical strike, preventing any evidence destruction.
Police Chief’s Statement: “This is just the beginning”
Buxar Superintendent of Police stated:
“We have dismantled a significant cyber crime module today.
Detailed forensic analysis will uncover the full extent of their reach and past crimes.
More arrests could follow soon.”
Their Modus Operandi — A Digital Trap
The gang followed a standard but dangerous pattern:
- Trigger fear — “Your bank account may be blocked”
- Send harmful links to gain phone access
- Coax users to reveal OTPs/UPI PINs
- Drain accounts instantly using online payment gateways
- Funnel money through multiple mule accounts to evade tracking
More Victims Expected to Come Forward
Digital evidence seized during the raid is being analysed to:
- Map inter-state connections
- Identify offshore betting apps and servers
- Track money flow and financial instruments
- Connect the syndicate with existing FIRs nationwide
Authorities expect that several cyber fraud complaints registered across India may now be linked to this racket.
Cyber Advisory Don’t Be the Next Victim
- Never click unknown links
- Do not share OTP/UPI PIN under any circumstance
- Banks or RBI officials never ask for confidential details
- Report suspicious cyber activity to National Helpline — 1930

- They’re easily scared and isolated.
- They’re less tech-savvy, making it easier to extract sensitive data and passwords.
How the scam works: 3 fear tactics
1. Threat to family’s life: Victims are told their family members will be harmed if they don’t comply. This emotional blackmail ensures silence and obedience.
2. Legal threats using PAN and Aadhaar misuse: Scammers claim that fake SIMs have been issued using Aadhaar, or that the PAN is linked to black money. Victims are warned of jail time if they don’t support the investigation.
3. Fake law enforcement setups: Fraudsters stage video calls with fake officers in uniforms and AI-generated courts, complete with judges and legal jargon. This "digital theatre" creates fear and urgency, prompting victims to follow instructions without question.
Case 1: Doctor couple from Patna duped of ₹1.95 crore
On May 21, 2025, Dr. Radhe Mohan received a call from someone posing as a CBI officer, claiming he and his wife, Chhavi were involved in a money laundering case tied to Naresh Goyal.
They were made to believe that a SIM card purchased using their Aadhaar had been used in crimes. Fake video calls followed, showing courts and police stations. In fear of arrest, the couple transferred ₹1.95 crore in six transactions via RTGS.
Status: ₹50 lakh has been frozen. However, tracking the money is challenging as it moved across 3–4 states.
Case 2: Retired professor cheated of ₹3.07 crore
On November 5, 2024, 78-year-old Professor Jyoti Verma got a call claiming fraudulent activity on a State Bank credit card. Soon, another fake CBI officer took over the call and said she was involved in laundering linked to the Naresh Goyal case.
The fraudsters showed her a fake digital arrest warrant and claimed she would face criminal action unless she transferred money. The elderly professor was kept on video call “house arrest” and manipulated into transferring ₹3.07 crore.
Status: Police have issued warrants against two people linked to the accounts where the money was transferred.
Case 3: Gaya doctor loses ₹4.4 crore in 4 days
On August 18, 2024, senior doctor Dr. NN Rai from Gaya received a call from a fake CBI officer. He was told that large sums of black money were detected in his bank accounts and that he could be arrested.
The doctor, terrified, complied with their instructions and transferred ₹4.4 crore across various accounts over four days.
Status: Only ₹15 lakh has been recovered. Another ₹60 lakh was reportedly on hold, but no updates have been shared due to police personnel transfers and delays in case handling.
Rise in digital arrest cases in Bihar
- 301 digital arrest cases were reported to the National Cyber Crime Helpline in 2024.
- Over ₹10 crore was stolen from victims.
- Cyber Cell has managed to freeze and seize more than ₹1.5 crore so far.
70 major frauds of ₹50 lakh or more
Between 2022 and June 10, 2025:
- Over 70 major frauds involving amounts over ₹50 lakh have been recorded.
- Total losses in these cases are estimated at ₹75 crore.
- Patna reported the highest number with 30 major cases, followed by Muzaffarpur, Purnea, Jehanabad, Motihari, and Samastipur.
Why police struggle to catch criminals
According to Cyber DSP Raghvendra Mani Tripathi:
- Fraudsters use fake accounts and IP addresses from multiple states, making tracking difficult.
- Weak interstate coordination between police units slows down investigations.
- Many fraudsters allegedly convert stolen funds into cryptocurrency, making recovery even harder.
Police suspect that a significant part of this money is being funneled to Arab countries through digital currency conversions. However, they remain tight-lipped about this on record.
What is Digital Arrest?
A new-age cybercrime, "digital arrest" involves:
- Posing as law enforcement officers
- Scaring people with fake arrest threats
- Using video calls, forged documents, and AI visuals
- Extracting large sums of money under the guise of cooperation in legal investigations
The Union Home Ministry has warned citizens to remain cautious of such scams and to never trust calls from unknown numbers claiming to be from ED, CBI, or police.
As cybercriminals evolve, the elderly and digitally unaware remain easy targets. The digital arrest scam is one of the most dangerous trends, combining technology, impersonation, and psychological fear. Authorities are urging citizens to stay informed, verify every legal threat, and immediately report suspicious calls to the Cyber Crime Helpline (1930).

title: 12 SSC candidates among 35 jailed for exam malpractice in Bihar - The Times of India
article_text:
Patna: As many as 35 people, arrested on Thursday for their alleged involvement in malpractices during central Staff Selection Commission (SSC) Multi-Tasking Staff examination in Purnia district, were forwarded to jail by a local court on Friday. They include 12 impostors, seven employees of the examination centre concerned, 12 candidates and the man in whose rented house there were hiding.
Police recovered Rs 4.2 lakh cash, three laptops, a printer, four vehicles, 52 Aadhar cards, 18 cellphones, 22 ATM cards, 12 blank cheques and 40 e-admit cards from their possession.
Purnia superintendent of police (SP) Kartikeya Kumar Sharma said a Katihar-based gang is suspected to be the mastermind of the exam racket. "During investigation, it was revealed that deals for dummy candidates or impostors were made for Rs 10.5 lakh from each aspirant. The impostors were promised Rs 2 lakh for passing the examination for the real candidates, while Rs 25,000 was paid to them in advance. The centre supervisor was also given Rs 1 lakh for each candidate through a cheque."
Sharma added that the activity of the flying squad, formed for inspection of the exam centre, is also suspicious. "They visited the exam centre for a very short time. Further investigation is going on in the matter."
According to police sources, Vivek, a native of Patna, and Roshan from Katihar are suspected to be the mastermind of the racket. They also allegedly run six online examination centres in Patna.
On Thursday, the police had received a tip-off that several impostors were giving the examination in place of real candidates at a centre on Gulabbagh-Hansda Road in Purnia Sadar police station area. "A raiding team was formed and sent to the Purnia Digital Examination Centre. Upon inspection, 12 impostors were identified as their biometric data did not match the records," the SP said.
According to the police, the 12 original candidates and two others were found hiding in the rented house of Suresh Chandra.
"During interrogation, the arrested candidates revealed that they were accommodated in various hotels in Purnia. The impostors were made to appear in the exam with the collusion of the institution's staff. Using a fake cable network from the adjacent building, they manipulated the fake biometric system to check in and out of the examination centre during the exam period. The original documents of the real candidates were also recovered from the building," Sharma said.
Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff and Havaldar (CBIC and CBN) exams were being conducted at the centre since September 30 in three shifts from 8am to 5pm. The test was of one-and-a-half hours, comprising 90 questions covering maths, reasoning, general studies and English.
"One of the impostors was appearing in the examination for the fourth time consecutively. Some had appeared two to three times earlier, while one was appearing for the first time," the SP said.
The Puirnia SP added that the racket involves an organised gang, including the examination lab owner. "Continuous raids are being carried out at various locations to identify others involved in this fraud."

title: Donald Trump's fake Indian residential certificate application surfaces in Bihar - Gulf News
article_text:
Officials believe the act was carried out to ridicule and defame the administrative system
In a bizarre twist to the growing trend of fake residence certificate cases in Bihar, an application has surfaced in Samastipur district seeking a certificate in the name of US President Donald Trump.
The incident took place in the Mohiuddinnagar zone, where an unidentified person submitted an online application using Trump’s photo and name, falsely listing the address as Village Hasanpur, Ward No. 13, Post Bakarpur, Police Station Mohiuddinnagar, District Samastipur.
The application, submitted on July 29, 2025, was recorded under Application No. BRCCO/2025/17989735.
Upon verification, officials found clear tampering in the form’s photo, Aadhaar number, barcode, and address details, prompting the Circle Officer (CO) to reject the application outright.
Officials believe the act was deliberately carried out to ridicule and defame the administrative system.
Mohiuddinnagar CO confirmed that this is a serious violation under the IT Act, and a complaint has been filed with the local cyber police station.
“Strict legal action will be taken against those responsible,” said the CO, adding that cybercrime investigators are now tracking the IP address and login credentials used in the prank.
This incident is the latest in a series of fake residence certificate scams surfacing across Bihar in recent weeks.
Officials have flagged previous applications under names like ‘Dog Babu’, ‘Nitish Kumari’, and even in the name of Sonalika tractor, in Patna, East Champaran, Nalanda and other districts of Bihar, exposing glaring loopholes in the online application verification system.
The repeated misuse of the online portal has raised serious concerns over digital document integrity and identity fraud.
Administrative officers are now considering technical audits and stricter KYC verification mechanisms to prevent further embarrassment.
As the state heads into election season, such incidents not only undermine the government’s digital governance claims but also highlight the urgent need for cyber vigilance and stronger administrative filters.

title: Bihar Topper Scam Fallout: Bihar Board mulls digital evaluation of Class X and XII answer sheets - India.Com
article_text:
After last year’s toppers scam in which the class XII topper’s Humanities topper Ruby Rai, Science topper Saurabh Shrestha and third topper in Science stream Rahul Kumar were caught after they failed to answer basic questions related to their subjects, the Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB) has decided to go the digital way to avoid tampering of the results. As per a report in DNA, approximately 2.80 lakh copies have been digitally evaluated. The year the Bihar board in order to ensure transparency trained the evaluators about the digital marking system.
This year the BSEB board followed a strict procedure. After the students wrote their papers, their answer sheets were bar-coded to avoid identification. Then the answer sheets were scanned using high-speed scanners, and the soft copies reached the computerised evaluation centres. The hard-copies were locked in strongrooms. This year specific pre- and post-exam software for tabulation and preparation of results and for facilitating the process has used by BSEB board. This year the results are likely to be declared by December 19. Students will also be able to access to their results through text messages and by email ID. title: Bihar: Digital arrest scam busted in Muzaffarpur; three arrested - thecolumns.in
Bihar: Digital arrest scam busted in Muzaffarpur; three arrested - Social News XYZ
article_text:
Patna, May 1 (SocialNews.XYZ) In a major breakthrough against cybercrime, the Cyber Police Station in Muzaffarpur has dismantled an organised gang involved in defrauding victims through the so-called “digital arrest” scam.
The action was initiated following a written complaint by a senior citizen who was cheated of Rs 17 lakh through intimidation and psychological pressure.
The victim, Bhola Prasad Mahto (73), a resident of Mushahari, reported that from April 5, 2026, he received multiple video calls from individuals posing as police and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officers.
The fraudsters allegedly threatened him with a “digital arrest”, creating fear and mental distress.
Under pressure, the victim transferred Rs 17 lakh via RTGS on April 10 to a bank account held by Brajesh Kumar at a Federal Bank branch in Bhagwanpur.
He realised he had been duped on April 13 and promptly reported the matter to his bank and the national cybercrime helpline (1930).
Taking the complaint seriously, police registered Case No. 58/26 and formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) under the direction of senior officials.
Through technical surveillance, call detail analysis and scrutiny of bank transactions, three accused were arrested. They have been identified as Brajesh Kumar, Krishna Kumar and Vikram Kumar.
The arrests mark a significant step in cracking down on emerging cyber fraud tactics.
During the operation, police recovered mobile phones, chequebooks, passbooks and debit cards from their possession.
Preliminary investigation revealed that the bank accounts used in this case were linked to multiple cyber fraud incidents across the country, indicating a wider network.
Police suspect that the gang operates at an inter-state level and has been targeting victims using evolving scam techniques such as “digital arrest”.
Continuous raids are underway to apprehend other members who remain absconding.
Authorities have urged citizens to remain alert and cautious. People have been advised not to trust unsolicited calls or video calls from individuals claiming to be police, the CBI or other officials.

article_text:
Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The investigation into the Rs 2.26 crore fraud involving the District Urban Development Agency (DUDA) on Friday uncovered a suspected inter-state gang operating across Bihar and Jharkhand.
Police said the suspects siphoned off funds using forged signatures of senior officials and later withdrew the money through ATMs at multiple locations in both states.
According to the Cyber Crime Branch, the fraud was executed through a well-planned strategy. The perpetrators allegedly used forged documents to link their own mobile numbers and email IDs to the official bank account, enabling them to intercept transaction alerts and gain unauthorised access.
After securing digital control, the gang transferred Rs2,26,71,000 through fake cheques into several shell accounts across states. These accounts were then used by accomplices to withdraw cash from ATMs, minimising traceable digital evidence.
Police confirmed that a key breakthrough came from CCTV footage at a Bank of India branch on Saifia College Road, which captured a suspect believed to be part of the network.
Investigators are now using facial recognition and intelligence inputs to identify him and track the wider syndicate. Meanwhile, police said three suspects have reportedly been detained for questioning. They are believed to have facilitated the opening and use of bank accounts.
Interrogation is expected to lead investigators to the mastermind behind the operation soon.

Mussoorie Station House Officer Devendra Chauhan stated that the questioning revealed the young man is highly educated and currently employed by a private company. title: You're selected: Fake UPSC result on Whatsapp sends Bihar man to IAS academy - India Today
article_text:
You're selected: Fake UPSC result on Whatsapp sends Bihar man to IAS academy
A Bihar man reached the IAS training academy in Mussoorie after receiving a fake UPSC selection letter on WhatsApp, only to discover he had been duped in a recruitment scam, prompting a police investigation.
What was meant to be the beginning of a dream career in the civil services turned into a shocking ordeal for a man from Bihar after he reached India's premier IAS training academy with a forged UPSC selection letter, only to discover he had been cheated.
The incident has exposed a disturbing scam in which fraudsters are luring aspirants with fake results and collecting money in the name of civil service recruitment.
REACHED IAS ACADEMY WITH A DREAM
Pushpesh Singh, a resident of Saran district in Bihar and an employee at a private firm in Gurugram, arrived at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA) in Mussoorie on Saturday, believing he had been selected for the prestigious Indian Administrative Service.
However, when academy officials verified his documents, they found that the UPSC result letter he carried was forged.
The academy administration immediately alerted the Mussoorie Police, following which senior police officials, along with teams from the Local Intelligence Unit and the Intelligence Bureau, reached the premises.
HOW THE SCAM UNFOLDED
During preliminary questioning, Singh revealed that he had come into contact with a group of people in Gurugram who promised to "manage" his civil service examination and interview.
According to the police, Singh paid Rs 13,000 in cash and Rs 14,564 through UPI in two instalments to people who claimed they would help him clear the civil service examination.
Later, the fraudsters sent him a fake UPSC result on WhatsApp that falsely declared him selected and instructed him to report to the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration in Mussoorie for training.
Trusting the message, Singh travelled to Mussoorie with his parents and luggage, convinced that he was about to begin his life as a civil servant.
TRUTH COMES OUT AT THE ACADEMY GATES
It was only after reaching the academy that the harsh reality surfaced.
Officials at LBSNAA informed him that no such selection existed. Realising he had been duped, Singh complained to the police.
"Prima facie, the man is a victim of organised fraud. He was misled with forged documents and false promises," a police officer was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.
ZERO FIR REGISTERED, PROBE SHIFTED TO GURUGRAM
Based on Singh's complaint, the police registered a zero FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Since the alleged fraud took place in Gurugram, the case has been transferred there for further investigation.
Authorities are now working to identify and trace the individuals who orchestrated the scam.
The incident highlights a worrying trend of recruitment-related fraud targeting aspirants desperate to crack competitive examinations like the UPSC Civil Services.
Police have urged UPSC civil services aspirants to rely only on official UPSC websites and authorised notifications for information, avoid falling for agents or middlemen who claim to "guarantee" selection, and immediately report any suspicious offers or messages to the authorities to prevent such frauds.

title: Bihar Police Files New Case Against Bank Manager In Rs 31 Crore Scam - Outlook Money
article_text:
In a case involving the fraudulent transfer of Rs 31.93 crore from the District Land Acquisition Officer’s (DLAO) bank account in Bihar, enforcement agencies are investigating forgery and money laundering. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) earlier took a bank's branch manager into custody and provisionally attached assets valued at Rs 1.66 crore. Recently, Bihar Police’s Economic Offences Unit (EOU) lodged a fresh FIR connected to the matter.
According to the Economic Times, the accused used forged documents and fake signatures to transfer funds over two years. To cover his tracks, he opened 21 fake accounts using the Aadhaar and KYC details of bank customers. The stolen money was laundered through foreign entities linked to South Africa and the Philippines and diverted to banned gambling apps. The branch manager was granted bail after being produced before the local court. The ED's investigation into money laundering is ongoing. Following findings, Bihar Police filed a new FIR on June 27, 2025.
According to reports, the branch manager hired money mules, giving incentives to those who used their bank accounts and UPI IDs to transfer the stolen funds, allowing him to hide his identity from investigators.
According to official ED documents, the inquiry began after Patna Police filed a formal complaint. On July 10, 2023, the branch manager was taken into custody by the Enforcement Directorate under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Preliminary attachments were made to assets valued at Rs 1.66 crore, and valuables worth Rs 1.38 crore were recovered during searches conducted at multiple locations. In January 2025, the ED continued its investigation and seized some more assets as part of the investigation. Some other accused have been arrested, and prosecution complaints have been filed.
The new FIR expands the probe to include money laundering accusations, forgery and official diversion of funds. Officials continue to attempt to trace the money and determine if anyone else was involved. The case has also drawn attention to client verification procedures and the monitoring of high-value transactions, indicating the need for stronger safeguards to protect public funds.
Some reports said that the manager worked with Kotak Mahindra Bank to which the bank reacted.
“The incident dating back to 2021 was proactively identified by Kotak Mahindra Bank through its internal monitoring systems. The employee involved was terminated from employment with the Bank, and the matter was reported to the authorities. The Bank's reporting and cooperation with the law enforcement agencies led to the arrest of the individual and the recovery of a substantial portion of the funds. We continue to pursue the matter through appropriate legal channels. The case remains sub judice.
While the investigators appear to have uncovered links to online betting platforms, the Bank had no involvement or visibility into these external activities since the activity relates to utilisation, by the ex-employee, of the proceeds from the fraud.
Kotak Mahindra Bank remains committed to strong governance, robust compliance practices, and the highest standards of customer protection.”

title: 16 cybercriminals from Bihar held in Bokaro - The Times of India
article_text:
Bokaro: The district police arrested 16 cybercriminals staying as tenants in two houses under the Sector-12 police station limits on Monday.
The arrested who posed as employees of courier companies are from Nalanda, Nawada, Jamui, Sheikhpura and other districts of Bihar and in the age group of 18-30 years. “Apart from documents related to cybercrime, fake notes of Rs 100 and Rs 200 denominations have also been recovered from them,” said DSP Kuldeep Kumar.
The arrest came after SP Priyadarshi Alok had received information about cybercrimes being carried out by some outsiders living in rented houses around Bari Cooperative. Police then raided the two houses. “Five people were caught from Bari Cooperative and 11 from a house in Manmohan Cooperative Colony,” said the DSP.
Documents related to cyber crime and many items like mobile phones, fake notes, pamphlets and offer letters have been recovered from them. During interrogation, the gang members said they cheated people through social media posts in the name of providing PM Mudra loan. The scammers would also target individuals who make online purchases, obtaining their data to orchestrate a lottery scam. In the process, victims received a deceptive winner letter and coupon via courier, featuring a helpline number and a scratch-off bar code. Upon contacting the helpline, linked to the scammers, victims were manipulated into paying substantial amounts for processing fees and GST, under the guise of claiming a non-existent prize, ranging from vehicles to cash.
The gang revealed the name of their kingpin is Sumit who resides in Patna.
Those arrested are Chandan Kumar, Vikram Kumar, Niwas Kumar, Sandeep Kumar, Vishal Kumar, Sanjay Kumar, Kanhaiya Kumar, Ranjeet Kumar, Praveen Kumar, Jitendra Kumar, Omprakash Kumar, Rajesh Bharti, Sanjeev Kumar, Dilkhush Kumar, Piyush Parasar and Jitendra Kumar.

title: Bihar youth held for floating fake UP home guard exam papers - The Times of India
article_text:
Lucknow: The UP STF on Saturday night arrested a Class XII passout for allegedly running an online fraud racket that duped aspirants by circulating fake question papers of the UP home guards recruitment examination. The exam was held recently.
The accused, Nikhil Thakur, 27, was arrested from a library premises in Bihar’s Muzaffarpur following sustained surveillance and intelligence inputs.
Nikhil, a native of Muzaffarpu, was wanted in a case registered at Lucknow’s Hussainganj police station under Sections of BNS, IT Act, and the UP Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Ordinance.
DSP, STF, Sudhanshu Shekhar, said Nikhil operated a well-organised digital racket along with an accomplice, Siddharth Mishra.
“The duo created multiple Telegram channels using virtual numbers to avoid detection and began targeting candidates preparing for the home guards written examination held between Apr 25 and 27,” said the officer.
Shekhar said the accused floated “leaked” and “100% confirmed” question papers on these channels to gain the trust of aspirants.
“Once candidates engaged, they were asked to pay hefty sums through UPI IDs and QR codes in exchange for access to the purported papers or assured success in the exam,” he said.
The accused exploited exam pressure and urgency. Many aspirants, fearing failure, transferred money believing the papers were genuine,” an STF officer said.
Police seized two mobile phones from the accused, which are now being analysed for chat records, transaction details and links to other victims. Preliminary findings suggest that several candidates may have been cheated across multiple districts.
The STF has launched a search for the co-accused and is expanding the probe to identify the full extent of the network. The accused is being brought to Lucknow for further legal proceedings.

title: Can’t allow Nawada to become another Jamtara: HC - The Times of India
article_text:
Patna: In a striking courtroom moment on Oct 21, 2021, Justice Sandeep Kumar of the Patna high court issued a remark that would set the tone for Bihar's battle against cybercrime: "This court cannot allow Nawada to become another Jamtara."The comment came during the hearing of an anticipatory bail plea filed by one Shiv Kumar, accused of vishing fraud, a form of cybercrime where victims are manipulated into revealing confidential banking details over phone calls. The case was registered at the Warisaliganj police station in Nawada, a district increasingly associated with digital scams.
Justice Kumar's observation was not offhand. It was, in fact, grounded in experience. The court had witnessed a growing number of cybercrime complaints emanating from Nawada and neighbouring districts such as Nalanda, Sheikhpura and Patna. What followed was a judicial nudge that became a full-blown directive.
In response to Shiv Kumar's case, the high court ordered the superintendents of police in the affected districts to form special investigation teams (SITs). These were to be made up of tech-savvy officers and cyber experts with the cooperation of the state's Economic Offences Unit (EOU). Their mission: to unearth the dens of cybercriminals and dismantle the digital scam networks spreading like wildfire.
Then, in a order dated Feb 1, 2022, the court took things a step further. It directed district SPs across Bihar to hold monthly meetings with officers from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and income tax (IT) Department. The goal? To trace and act upon the ill-gotten assets of cybercriminals using provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and the Income Tax Act.
Justice Kumar, acutely aware of internal leakages in the banking system, also pointed fingers at those entrusted with the public's financial security. "In the opinion of this Court, any cyberfraud is committed by the cyber criminals only after the bank account details, phone numbers of account holders are leaked by the bank employees," he remarked.
In response, he directed the higher officials of public sector banks and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to tighten internal vigilance. Bank personnel found leaking customer data, he said, must be treated as accomplices to the crime.
The concern was not just theoretical. Between Dec 2021 and March 2022, several advocates of the Patna high court came forward with complaints of cyberfraud with many accusing the police of inaction. One particularly shocking case involved advocate Manindra Kishore Singh, whose fixed deposit of over Rs 4 lakh was siphoned off directly from the SBI branch within the high court premises.
The judiciary was visibly displeased. The EOU was ordered to intensify its crackdown and push enforcement to its "hardest extent."
Realising the broader public threat, the High Court also directed the state to roll out a comprehensive awareness campaign. The message, spread across electronic, print and social media: never share banking details over the phone.
On March 21 last year, another voice from the bench echoed these concerns. While denying bail to Anand Kumar and five others accused of cybercrime, Justice Ramesh Chand Malviya did not mince words:
"Cybercrime is a growing menace in India," he said, citing central govt data. "Around 65,893 cases were registered in 2022, marking a 24.4% increase from the 52,974 cases reported in 2021. Looking at the vast picture of online frauds and cybercrimes in recent times, it seems there is hardly anyone left who hasn't been targeted," he added.
Justice Malviya stressed that the police must leave no stone unturned in investigating such cases. He called for comprehensive call detail record (CDR) analysis, IP log tracing and supporting documentation to build "foolproof cases" against perpetrators.
The Patna high court's proactive approach, marked by stinging observations and concrete directives, has lit a fire under Bihar's enforcement machinery. What began as a single bail hearing has since evolved into a broader reckoning with the digital underworld.

title: ₹150cr fraud: Gang busted, 6 from UP, Bihar & Hry in net - The Times of India
article_text:
Gurgaon: An investment fraud racket has been busted with the arrest of six people from UP, Bihar and Haryana. A total of Rs 150 crore fraudulent transactions have taken place through bank accounts linked to the accused during the last six months and Rs 15 crore defrauded amount has gone into crypto accounts operated by Chinese nationals.
The search for the accused started when on Nov 30 last year, a man lodged a complaint at Cyber east police station that he had been duped of Rs 8.5 lakh through task based investment fraud.
According to cyber crime ACP Priyanshu Dewan and inspector Jasvir Singh, the victim received a part-time job offer message on WhatsApp and after a payment of paltry sum for liking videos online, he was offered to invest in prepaid tasks to receive better returns.
“However, during the transactions, the accused kept asking for deposits from the ‘employee’ in the name of different taxes, duties and commissions . After losing Rs 8.5 lakh to the fraudsters, the victim approached the cops,” the ACP said.
The first accused — Utkarsh — was arrested from Prayagraj on Feb 14. Utkarsh is a goldsmith.
After his confession, cops arrested his friend, Ashutosh, a student from Gopal Gunj in Bihar on Feb 18, who in turn provided details of Chander Prakash Tiwari of Sugar Mill Colony in Kaithal. Chander Prakash, a high school dropout, was allegedly involved in gambling cases. He, along with his associates Nitin Kumar, Abhinav and Ankit were caught on Feb 22.
Police found out that in the past six months, transactions amounting to Rs 150 crore have taken place through the seven bank accounts linked to the six arrested accused. A significant amount from the bank accounts was used to purchase crypto currency by a Dubai based operator and about Rs 15 crore in the form of crypto has been transferred to the wallets linked to a Chinese national.
Police seized three cell phones and four banking kits from the possession of the accused. The details of the accused will be run through ‘linkage analysis’ feature of Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to identify exactly in how many cases they were involved in.

title: e-challan in Bihar: How to Check and Pay Online - ACKO Drive
article_text:
The e-challan system in Bihar is a digital initiative aimed at modernising traffic enforcement across the state. Introduced by the Bihar Traffic Police, this system replaces traditional paper challans with electronic versions, allowing citizens to conveniently pay fines online. With its focus on transparency and efficiency, the e-challan system in Bihar streamlines the process of issuing and paying fines, making traffic management more efficient and reducing paperwork.
In this article, we delve into the workings of the e challan Bihar, and its benefits, and provide step-by-step guides on how to check and pay e-challans through platforms like the Parivahan portal and the Bihar Traffic Police website.
Contents
What is e-challan?
An e-challan is an electronically generated challan, or fine slip, issued by traffic authorities for violating traffic rules. Unlike traditional paper-based challans, e-challans are part of a broader effort to digitise and streamline traffic enforcement. When a traffic violation is detected, either by traffic officers or automatically through surveillance cameras, an e-challan is generated and linked to the vehicle’s registration number.
The system notifies the violator, often via SMS, detailing the offence, the location, and the fine amount. The e-challan system is integrated with online portals like the Parivahan website and state-specific websites, where violators can check their e-challan status, view past violations, and pay fines conveniently. This digital approach enhances transparency, reduces paperwork, and simplifies the process for both traffic authorities and the public.
How Does the System of e-challan Work?
The e-challan system is a digital approach to managing traffic violations, designed to streamline the enforcement process and enhance transparency. Here’s how it operates:
Violation Detection: Traffic violations are detected through two main methods: manually by traffic officers using handheld devices or automatically through CCTV cameras installed at intersections and key locations. These devices capture essential details such as the vehicle’s registration number, type of violation, location, and time.
Issuance of e-challan: Once a violation is recorded, an e-challan is generated instantly. If detected manually, officers input the information into a digital device, which then issues the e-challan. For violations detected by CCTV, the system processes the footage, verifies the violation, and generates the e-challan linked to the vehicle’s registration number.
Notification to the Violator: After the e-challan is issued, a notification is sent to the violator’s registered mobile number. This SMS includes details about the violation, the fine amount, and payment instructions, ensuring the violator is promptly informed.
Tracking and Payment: Violators can track their e-challan status through platforms like the Parivahan portal or state-specific websites. By entering details like the vehicle number or challan number, they can view any pending fines and make payments online using options like UPI, debit/credit cards, or net banking.
Payment Confirmation: Once the payment is processed, a digital receipt is generated, and a confirmation message is sent to the violator’s mobile number. The e-challan system updates the status in real time, marking the violation as resolved. This receipt serves as proof of payment and can be saved for future reference.
Advantages of Paying e-challan in Bihar
The following advantages make paying e-challans in Bihar more efficient and user-friendly, promoting compliance with traffic laws and contributing to improved road safety across the state.
Convenience and Time-Saving: The e-challan system allows users to pay fines from anywhere, eliminating the need for in-person visits to traffic stations. This convenience saves time, reduces travel, and makes the process more accessible to residents across Bihar.
24/7 Access: The online system is accessible around the clock, allowing violators to handle their fines at any time, day or night. This flexibility ensures that payments can be made without being limited to traditional office hours.
Enhanced Transparency: Each e-challan provides clear information on the offence, including details such as the date, time, location, and type of violation. This transparency helps violators understand the charges and reduces any confusion or disputes over fines.
Multiple Payment Options: e-challans can be paid using a variety of secure payment methods, including debit/credit cards, UPI, and net banking. These options make it easy for users to complete payments online, eliminating the need for cash transactions.
Environmentally Friendly: As a digital initiative, the e-challan system reduces the need for paper, supporting eco-friendly practices and aligning with Bihar’s commitment to sustainability by moving away from physical challan slips.
How to Check e-challan Status in Bihar
You can easily check your e-challan status in Bihar through the State Government Portal, Parivahan Website, or the ACKO App. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to use each platform:
1. Bihar State Government Portal
You can quickly check the status of your e-challan through the official Bihar Police website. Here’s how:
Step 1: Visit the official Bihar State Government e-challan portal.
Step 2: Go to the E-Challan or Challan Status section.
Step 3: Enter your vehicle registration number, challan number, or driving licence number.
Step 4: Complete the Captcha and click on Search.
Step 5: The page will display all pending and paid e-challans linked to your vehicle.
2. Parivahan Website
The Parivahan Sewa portal from the Government of India is another platform to check your e-challan status. Follow these steps:
Step 1: Open the Parivahan e-challan portal at echallan.parivahan.gov.in.
Step 2: Click on Check Challan Status on the homepage.
Step 3: Enter your vehicle number, challan number, or driving licence (DL) number.
Step 4: Click on Get Details to view your e-challan status.
Step 5: The portal will display any pending fines, including details of the violation, location, and fine amount.
3. ACKO App
If you’re looking for a more mobile-friendly option, the ACKO app provides an easy way to check your e-challan status. Here’s how to use it:
Step 1: Open the ACKO app on your mobile device.
Step 2: Log in or create an account and go to the “Pay Traffic Challan” section.
Step 3: Enter your vehicle registration number and tap Search.
Step 4: The app will show all pending and cleared e-challans linked to your vehicle.
Step 5: Review any outstanding fines and proceed with payment if required.
How to Pay e-challan in Bihar
Paying your e-challan in Bihar is simple, with several online platforms available. Citizens can pay their fines through the Bihar State Government website, the Parivahan portal, or third-party apps like ACKO. Be cautious of e-challan scams, where fraudsters may send fake messages or emails requesting payment. Always confirm the authenticity of any communication before proceeding with payment. Below is a detailed guide on how to use each platform for e-challan payments.
1. Bihar State Government Portal
Step 1: Visit the official Bihar State Government e-challan portal.
Step 2: Go to the E-Challan Payment or Challan Status section.
Step 3: Enter your vehicle registration number, challan number, or driving license number to retrieve your e-challan.
Step 4: Select the e-challan you wish to pay.
Step 5: Proceed to payment and choose your preferred payment method, such as debit/credit card, UPI, or net banking.
Step 6: After completing the payment, download or save the digital receipt for reference.
2. Parivahan Website
Step 1: Go to the Parivahan e-challan portal at echallan.parivahan.gov.in.
Step 2: Click on Check Challan Status and enter your vehicle number, challan number, or driving licence (DL) number.
Step 3: Select the e-challan you want to pay.
Step 4: Proceed to payment using options like net banking, UPI, or debit/credit card.
Step 5: Save the confirmation receipt generated after payment for your records.
3. ACKO App
Step 1: Download and open the ACKO app on your smartphone.
Step 2: Log in or create an account, then navigate to the “Pay Traffic Challan” section.
Step 3: Enter your vehicle registration number and tap Search to view all pending challans.
Step 4: Select the e-challan(s) you wish to pay.
Step 5: Choose a payment method, such as UPI, debit/credit card, or digital wallet, to complete the transaction.
Step 6: Once payment is processed, you’ll receive a confirmation within the app and an SMS.

Conclusion
In conclusion, the e-challan system in Bihar is instrumental in improving traffic management by enhancing transparency, efficiency, and accountability. By digitalizing the issuance and payment of fines, the system reduces paperwork, streamlines enforcement, and provides timely notifications to violators. This promotes responsible driving habits and encourages prompt fine payment, helping drivers avoid additional penalties. Overall, the e-challan system in Bihar contributes to safer roads and a well-organised approach to traffic regulation, benefiting both authorities and citizens alike.
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are some of the most important question and their answer related to e-challan in Bihar
What happens if I don't pay a challan in Bihar?
If you don’t pay an e-challan, your vehicle registration may be suspended, your driving licence revoked, or even a warrant issued.
